summary: Full end-to-end testing completed on Multi-modal RAG Technical Support app. All 10 pytest backend tests passed (status, upload-pdf, upload-image, ask text-only, ask multimodal with Gemini vision, reset, and validation errors). Frontend UI flows verified: PDF upload -> index build (1 chunk shown), image upload with preview + remove button, ask flow with expandable Sources, and Reset clears chat + backend index. Gemini vision correctly identified 'ERROR E01 / OVERHEATING' text and red LED from the test image and referenced the actual manual content (15-minute cool down for E01) in the answer. No mocked APIs. AI capability (Gemini gemini-flash-latest) verified real end-to-end with real output.

minor.issue: CORS middleware is registered AFTER app.include_router(api), so preflight OPTIONS on API routes may not receive CORS headers depending on Starlette version. In practice the app works from the browser (verified in UI test), but recommended to add_middleware BEFORE include_router.
Errors from Gemini bubble up as generic 500 with 'Failed to get answer: <str(exc)>' — exposes provider internals. Consider a cleaner error contract for the client.
No size limit / content-type validation beyond extension check; user could upload a non-image file with a .jpg extension. PIL.Image.open would fail later inside /api/ask, producing a 500.

ui_bugs.issue: The 'x' remove button only appears on hover (opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100). On touch devices there is no way to remove an image. Consider making it always visible or add tap support.

issues: Markdown (## / ** **) is rendered as raw text because messages use whitespace-pre-wrap only; Gemini responds with Markdown formatting which shows literal '###' and '**' to the user. Consider a Markdown renderer (e.g., react-markdown).

action_items: (Nice-to-have) Render assistant messages with a Markdown renderer so headings/bold formatting from Gemini isn't shown as raw text.
(Nice-to-have) Make image remove button visible without hover for touch users.
(Nice-to-have) Validate uploaded image bytes with PIL at upload time to fail fast rather than at ask time.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py: CORS middleware added after include_router — safe in most Starlette versions but conventionally middleware should be added before mounting routers.

rag.py: get_context is called with default k=4 on every ask; if the index is empty, context is [] which is handled — good. But no upper bound on prompt size if manual is huge (all top-k chunks concatenated).

pdf_loader.chunk_text: chunk size measured in words but overlap is subtracted from index (i += size - overlap), so overlap is by word count, not tokens — acceptable but could produce very small chunks for large 'words' (e.g., long URLs).

gemini.py: creates a single global client at import time — if GEMINI_API_KEY is missing the module still imports and only fails on call (RuntimeError). Consider surfacing a clear 503 at startup instead.
Frontend App.js: `URL.createObjectURL(file)` blobs are never revoked — small memory leak on repeated uploads.
Frontend App.js: Errors are shown as a small red line but the user can't dismiss them and they can be overwritten silently by the next action.
No pagination / size limit on messages state; long chat could grow unbounded (acceptable for session-only).
seed_data_creation: Created /app/test_fixtures/sample_manual.pdf (real 2-page technical support manual PDF with power/wifi/error-code sections) and /app/test_fixtures/product.jpg (real 640x480 JPEG of a mock device displaying 'ERROR E01 OVERHEATING' with red LED and physical buttons — non-uniform, real visual features).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend at https://support-ai-mentor.preview.emergentagent.com. Run `pytest /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py` — 10 tests, ~15s. Uses fixtures in /app/test_fixtures. Gemini gemini-flash-latest works with the key in backend/.env. Test image intentionally has visible 'ERROR E01' text so Gemini vision assertions can verify multimodal grounding.
rca_of_the_issue: No blocking issues found. Only minor UX/code-quality suggestions listed above.
